title: In the JRA-3Q twin reanalysis (1985-1990), a 0.08 C warmer SST boundary raises net downward TOA radiation by 0.15 W m-2 through less low cloud; a free-model Green's function gives the opposite sign
abstract: JMA changed the SST boundary of the JRA-3Q reanalysis in June 1985 from COBE-SST2 to MGDSST and made a twin run (JRA-3Q-COBE, June 1985-December 1990) with the same model and observations. We use the twin difference as a clean test of how a data-assimilating system responds to an SST boundary change. The ocean-mean SST boundary is 0.052 C warmer (ice-free ocean 60S-60N: +0.081 C). The global net downward TOA radiation increases by +0.155 +/- 0.026 W m-2 (absorbed solar +0.278, outgoing longwave +0.123), or +3.0 +/- 0.5 W m-2 per K. The ECHAM6 Green's function (Zenodo 18840026) predicts -0.115 W m-2 for the same SST change; it gets the longwave part right but not the shortwave part. The mechanism is the assimilation constraint: the analysed 700 hPa temperature rises only 13% as much as the SST (Jan-Aug 1990), stability falls by 0.10 K, low cloud decreases by 0.38 percentage points (-3.4 points per K on 10-degree blocks, r = -0.59), and absorbed solar follows low cloud (r = -0.85). The first-guess 2 m air temperature keeps 70% of the SST change, the analysis 27%. At 105 tropical moorings (1990-2026), buoy air-sea difference has no trend, but the JRA-3Q first guess warms 0.036 (0.014-0.062) C per decade faster than buoy air, so a first-guess correction of JRA-3Q marine air can overstate tropical warming. The June 1985 SST step is +0.071 to +0.099 C against all 200 HadSST4 members. Limitations: one reanalysis and a GF from a different model; low cloud uses 24 months and 700 hPa temperature 8 months; TOA fluxes are model forecasts. Implication: SST-boundary errors give reanalysis TOA and cloud artifacts with a sign that free-model Green's functions do not give. No third-party data are in the bundle (JRA-3Q is CC BY-NC-SA); scripts regenerate all numbers.

display.caption: JRA-3Q minus JRA-3Q-COBE (only the SST/ice boundary differs): ocean-mean SST change, global TOA changes, and the ECHAM6 Green's-function prediction. The twin absorbs more solar radiation; the GF predicts net cooling.
Mechanism: low cloud decreases where the SST boundary is warmer, the analysed 700 hPa temperature hardly changes, and absorbed solar follows low cloud on 10-degree blocks.
Trends of differences at 105 tropical moorings, 1990-2026: the JRA-3Q first guess warms faster than buoy air; ship and buoy air agree.
